robots_txt_adjudication.question: The executor departed from the shipped split-stance robots.txt template on the grounds that it is wrong. Adjudicate on the specification.
robots_txt_adjudication.version_assessed: The 61ac57a version — the one the executor worked against. Retrieved and re-verified at close with `git show 61ac57a:optimize/technical-seo-checker/references/robots-txt-reference.md`, lines 204-238, byte-identical to what this grader read and quoted before commit 9e5cd43 existed.
robots_txt_adjudication.verdict: THE EXECUTOR IS RIGHT AND THE SHIPPED TEMPLATE WAS WRONG. Stated plainly: at 4.5.0 this library shipped a paste-ready robots.txt that silently failed to protect the paths it appeared to protect, and it did so for the two most important search crawlers and six named AI agents.

reasoning.the_rule: RFC 9309 §2.2.1: a crawler matches the group whose user-agent line is the most specific match for its product token and obeys that group. Groups matching the SAME token are combined with each other; a named group is never combined with the `*` group. The wildcard applies only where NO named group matches: 'If no matching group exists, crawlers MUST obey the group with a user-agent line with the "*" value, if present.' Google's own robots.txt specification states the same in one sentence — only one group is valid for a particular crawler, and other groups are ignored.
reasoning.applied_to_the_shipped_block: The 4.5.0 split-stance example placed `Disallow: /admin/` and `Disallow: /private/` in the `User-agent: *` group ALONE. Above it sat four named groups: Googlebot and Bingbot with a bare `Disallow:`; OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot with a bare `Disallow:`; ChatGPT-User, Claude-User and Perplexity-User with a bare `Disallow:`. A bare `Disallow:` is allow-everything. Each of those eight agents matches its own group, obeys only that group, and never reaches the `*` rules. The file protected /admin/ and /private/ from unnamed crawlers and from nobody else — while reading, to the client pasting it, as though it protected them from everyone.
reasoning.why_this_is_not_a_judgement_call: The same reference file demonstrates correct understanding of group precedence 15 lines later. Configuration 5, 'Allow Search Engines, Block Everything Else' (lines 253-273), is correct precisely BECAUSE groups do not merge: it puts `Disallow: /` in `*` and bare `Disallow:` in the named groups, and works exactly as labelled. The file therefore does not hold a consistent-but-simplified model of the protocol; it applies the rule correctly in one template and inverts it in the other. That is an error, not a documented abstraction.
reasoning.severity_stated_honestly: Real but bounded, and worth stating precisely rather than dramatising. robots.txt is not an access control — the same reference says so at Mistake 5 ('If you don't want a page indexed, use noindex ... NOT robots.txt') — so the harm is crawl-budget waste and index exposure of utility paths, not a security breach. What makes it the most severe defect in this record is not the blast radius but the class: it is a paste-ready block, handed to a client with deploy-as-delivered framing, that is confidently wrong about the protocol it is written in, and no gate leg in this repo could have seen it. It is not a fence, a version, a link, a token or a claim shape.

A deliverable that copied the shipped shape would have added allow-all groups for those agents and thereby stopped blocking /checkout/ and /account/ for them — while e1.1 requires those blocks be KEPT. Both expectations would still have scored PASS on their text. The suite cannot see this defect.

It then states the rule for the client, twice, in the client's own terms — L225: 'The repetition is required: a crawler obeys only the most specific group that names it, and ignores `*` entirely once it has one — so a rule written only in `*` would not apply to Googlebot'; and L258 as a standing warning to whoever edits the file next: 'If someone later adds Disallow: /new-private-thing/ to the `*` group only, Googlebot, Bingbot and all six named AI agents will keep crawling it. Any new blanket rule goes in every group.' It also correctly declined to import /admin/ and /private/, which the fixture never mentions.
